pages.caption: A prince wanted to marry a princess, but one who was a real princess.
pages.scene: A castle with towers and flags. The prince stands at the gate in fine clothes. The road stretches behind him into the distance.

pages.caption: He went all over the world in search of one, but there was always something wrong.
pages.scene: A wide landscape of forests, mountains, and distant castles. The prince walks along a winding road with a satchel.

pages.caption: Princesses there were in plenty, but whether they were real princesses he could not quite make out.
pages.scene: A grand hall with chandeliers and mirrors. Many princesses in fine gowns stand around a throne. The prince looks uncertain.

pages.caption: There was always something which was not as it should be.
pages.scene: A throne room with a disappointed prince bowing to an elderly king on a golden throne. The prince's face shows sadness.

pages.caption: So he came home again, looking very sad, for he wanted very much to have a real princess.
pages.scene: The prince walks back through the castle gate at dusk. His shoulders are slumped and his expression is melancholy.

pages.caption: Now one stormy night there was a terrible knocking at the palace gate.
pages.scene: Dark storm clouds over the palace. Rain lashes the stone walls. Lightning flashes across a purple sky.

pages.caption: The old king went to open it, but what was his surprise to see a girl standing outside.
pages.scene: The palace gate with iron bars and torchlight. A young girl stands outside, soaked and bedraggled. Her hair drips with water.

pages.caption: Such a poor, bedraggled, wet creature! The water streamed from her hair and clothes.
pages.scene: Close view of the girl in rags. Water streams from her clothes. Her shoes are broken at the heels and toes.

pages.caption: It ran in at the heels of her shoes and out at the toes.
pages.scene: The girl's shoes with water running in at the heels and out at the toes. Puddles form on the stone floor.

pages.caption: But she said she was a real princess.
pages.scene: The girl looks up at the old king with earnest eyes. She speaks with quiet dignity despite her ragged appearance.

pages.caption: Well, we shall soon see about that, thought the old queen, but she said nothing.
pages.scene: The old queen in her chamber, looking thoughtful. She stands by a window with a knowing expression.

pages.caption: She went into the bedroom, took all the bed-clothes off the bed.
pages.scene: The queen in a bedroom with a large four-poster bed. She removes the bed-clothes with careful hands.

pages.caption: And put three little peas on the bottom.
pages.scene: Three small peas placed on the bare wooden slats of the bed frame. The queen's hands arrange them carefully.

pages.caption: Then she took twenty mattresses and laid them on the three peas.
pages.scene: Twenty mattresses stacked one upon another, forming a high tower of bedding. The queen adjusts the top layer.

pages.caption: And then twenty eider-down quilts on top of the mattresses.
pages.scene: Twenty eider-down quilts placed atop the mattresses. The bed is now impossibly high, reaching near the ceiling.

pages.caption: And this was the bed in which she was to sleep.
pages.scene: The finished bed, towering high. The queen stands beside it, satisfied. A ladder leans against the bed for climbing.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The girl climbing the ladder to the towering bed. Candlelight casts long shadows on the walls.

pages.caption: In the morning they asked her how she had slept.
pages.scene: Morning light through the window. The king and queen stand at the bedroom door. The girl sits up in the high bed, looking exhausted.

pages.caption: Oh, terribly! said she. I hardly closed my eyes all night long.
pages.scene: The girl descends the ladder, her body showing bruises. She holds her back in pain, her face drawn with discomfort.

pages.caption: I don't know what was in the bed, but I lay on something hard.
pages.scene: The girl gestures toward the bed, explaining her suffering. The king and queen listen with interest.

pages.caption: And it has made me black and blue all over my body. It was horrible!
pages.scene: The girl shows bruises on her arms and shoulders. The queen's expression shifts to understanding.

pages.caption: Then they knew that she was a real princess.
pages.scene: The king and queen exchange a knowing glance. The queen smiles knowingly. The girl watches them uncertainly.

pages.caption: For through the twenty mattresses and the twenty eider-down quilts she had felt the three peas.
pages.scene: The queen lifts the mattress corner, revealing the three peas still on the wooden slats below. Proof of the test.

pages.caption: So the prince married her, for he knew that he had found a real princess.
pages.scene: A grand wedding ceremony in a cathedral. The prince and princess stand at the altar, joined by clergy. Flowers adorn the pillars.

pages.caption: Now there was a servant in the palace who was very envious of the young queen.
pages.scene: A servant woman in the palace corridors, watching the royal couple from behind a tapestry. Her eyes are narrow with envy.

pages.caption: And she was a witch.
pages.scene: The servant woman alone in her room, her face transformed into a witch's cruel features. Dark magic swirls around her.

pages.caption: One day when the queen's first baby was born, the witch stole it.
pages.scene: The queen's bedchamber. A newborn baby lies in a cradle. The queen rests peacefully. The witch watches from the doorway.

pages.caption: And put a little changeling in its place.
pages.scene: The witch lifts the baby from the cradle with thin, claw-like hands. The queen sleeps unaware.

pages.caption: A little changeling, with a large head and a tiny body.
pages.scene: A changeling with a large head and tiny body lies in the cradle where the real baby was. It looks unnatural and wrong.

pages.caption: Then she flew away with the baby to an enchanted castle.
pages.scene: The witch flies through the night sky on a broomstick, clutching the stolen baby. The palace recedes below.

pages.caption: Where she set it down in a cradle.
pages.scene: A dark enchanted castle on a craggy mountain. The witch places the baby in a cradle inside its cold stone walls.

pages.caption: Next morning, when the servants came to look at the baby, they were horrified.
pages.scene: Morning. Servants enter the nursery and recoil in horror at the changeling in the cradle. Their hands cover their mouths.

pages.caption: To see a little changeling, with a large head and a tiny body.
pages.scene: Close view of the changeling â€” large head, tiny body, unnatural features. The servants whisper in fear.

pages.caption: They told the king, but he was so fond of the queen that he did not wish to grieve her.
pages.scene: The servants kneel before the king in his throne room. They gesture toward the nursery with fearful expressions.

pages.caption: He ordered the changeling to be well cared for.
pages.scene: The king sits on his throne, his face troubled. He considers the situation with care, stroking his beard.

pages.caption: And told the servants to say nothing to the queen.
pages.scene: The king leans forward, speaking sternly to the servants. His finger points for emphasis.

pages.caption: The next time the queen had a baby, the same thing happened.
pages.scene: Time passes. The queen holds a second newborn baby. She smiles lovingly. The witch watches from the shadows again.

pages.caption: And again the king had the changeling cared for.
pages.scene: The witch steals the second baby and replaces it with another changeling. The cradle holds the unnatural child.

pages.caption: And told the servants to be silent.
pages.scene: The king gestures for silence to the servants, his face drawn with worry. The changeling lies in the nursery.

pages.caption: But the third time, when the queen had a baby, the king himself watched by the door.
pages.scene: The queen cradles her third newborn. She gazes down with deep love. The room is warm with firelight.

pages.caption: And he saw the witch come and steal the baby.
pages.scene: The king hides behind the nursery door, peering through a crack. His eye is sharp with determination.

pages.caption: And put a changeling in its place.
pages.scene: The witch enters the nursery, her hands reaching for the baby. She places a changeling in the cradle.

pages.caption: Then the king had the witch seized.
pages.scene: The king bursts through the door, pointing accusingly at the witch. Guards rush in behind him with drawn swords.

pages.caption: And burned.
pages.scene: A pyre burns in the castle courtyard. The witch is consumed by flames. The king watches with grim resolve.

pages.caption: And the changeling was put to death.
pages.scene: The changeling lies lifeless. The nursery is quiet. The king stands alone, grief etched on his face.

pages.caption: But the three babies were still in the enchanted castle.
pages.scene: Three empty cradles in the nursery. The king and queen stand together, their faces heavy with sorrow.

pages.caption: The king and queen were very unhappy, for they did not know where their children were.
pages.scene: The king and queen sit in their chamber, heads bowed. The room is dim with grief. A candle flickers between them.

pages.caption: At last the king said he would go and search for them.
pages.scene: The king rises from his chair with determination. He clenches his fist, resolve hardening his features.

pages.caption: He took a bag of food and set out.
pages.scene: The king packs bread, cheese, and water into a leather bag. He places it over his shoulder.

pages.caption: He walked for many days.
pages.scene: The king walks through forests and over hills. The seasons change around him â€” leaves fall, snow comes, then melts.

pages.caption: And at last he came to a mountain. There he saw a giant's castle.
pages.scene: A massive mountain rises before the king. On its peak sits a giant's castle with iron gates and towers of black stone.

pages.caption: And he went in.
pages.scene: The king pushes open the iron gate and enters the castle courtyard. Shadows loom from the high walls.

pages.caption: In the kitchen was a girl who looked after everything for the giant.
pages.scene: A vast kitchen with a roaring fire and enormous pots. A beautiful girl tends the cooking, her face sad but determined.

pages.caption: She was very beautiful, but she was sad.
pages.scene: The girl turns to face the king. Her beauty is striking, but her eyes hold deep sadness.

pages.caption: The king asked her who she was.
pages.scene: The king approaches the girl in the kitchen. He looks at her questioningly. Steam rises from the cooking pots.

pages.caption: And she told him she was the Master-Maid, and that she had been stolen by the giant.
pages.scene: The girl stands before the king, her hands clasped. She speaks with quiet dignity despite her servant's clothes.

pages.caption: She said that the giant had three children who had been stolen from a king and queen.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid gestures toward the upper floors of the castle. She speaks in a hushed, urgent tone.

pages.caption: And that she had to look after them.
pages.scene: The king's face lights with recognition. His eyes widen and he steps forward eagerly.

pages.caption: The king was overjoyed, for he knew that these were his children.
pages.scene: The king clasps the Master-Maid's hands, overcome with emotion. Tears of hope fill his eyes.

pages.caption: The Master-Maid told him that he must wait until the giant was asleep.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid holds up a finger, signaling caution. She glances toward the giant's chamber upstairs.

pages.caption: And then she would help him to carry the children away.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid speaks urgently, her eyes darting to the staircase. The king listens intently.

pages.caption: She gave him a ball of thread.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid hands the king a ball of white thread. It glows faintly in the dim kitchen light.

pages.caption: And told him to tie one end of it to his wrist.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid demonstrates, tying one end of the thread around the king's wrist. Her movements are precise and careful.

pages.caption: And then she would lead him to the room where the children were.
pages.scene: The ball of thread rests in the king's palm. The Master-Maid points upward toward the castle's upper rooms.

pages.caption: The king did as she told him.
pages.scene: The giant sits at an enormous table, devouring whole roasted animals. His massive frame fills the chair.

pages.caption: And when the giant was asleep.
pages.scene: The giant yawns hugely, his massive mouth opening wide. His eyes grow heavy with sleep.

pages.caption: The Master-Maid led him to the room where the three children were.
pages.scene: The giant lies snoring on a stone slab bed. The castle trembles with each breath. The Master-Maid creeps past.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The Master-Maid leads the king up a dark spiral staircase. The thread trails behind them, glowing faintly.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: A small room at the top of the castle. Three children sleep in tiny beds. The Master-Maid opens the door gently.

pages.caption: He took them on his back.
pages.scene: The king sees his three children sleeping. His face breaks into tears of joy and relief. He reaches toward them.

pages.caption: And she led him out of the castle.
pages.scene: The king lifts the first child onto his back, then the second. The Master-Maid helps secure them.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The Master-Maid leads the king through dark corridors, past the sleeping giant's chamber. They move silently.

pages.caption: Then he ran away with the children.
pages.scene: The castle gate opens. The king steps into the night air with the children on his back. The Master-Maid holds the door.

pages.caption: And the Master-Maid went back to the castle.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid closes the gate softly and returns to the kitchen. Her face shows determination mixed with fear.

pages.caption: When the giant woke up.
pages.scene: Dawn breaks over the mountain. The giant wakes and stretches. He calls out for the children.

pages.caption: He was very angry to find that the children were gone.
pages.scene: The giant enters the children's room and finds the beds empty. His face contorts with rage.

pages.caption: He asked the Master-Maid what had happened.
pages.scene: The giant storms down to the kitchen, his massive footsteps shaking the stones. He towers over the Master-Maid.

pages.caption: And she told him that the king had come and taken them away.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid stands before the giant, her face calm but her hands trembling. She speaks steadily.

pages.caption: The giant was furious.
pages.scene: The giant's face turns purple with fury. He grabs a massive club and smashes a table in half.

pages.caption: And he set out to pursue the king.
pages.scene: The giant rushes out of the castle, club in hand. He scans the horizon and spots the king in the distance.

pages.caption: The king ran as fast as he could.
pages.scene: The king runs down the mountain path with the children on his back. He looks back in terror at the pursuing giant.

pages.caption: But the giant ran faster.
pages.scene: The giant bounds down the mountain, taking enormous strides. Each step covers what would take the king ten.

pages.caption: At last the king came to a river, and he could not get across.
pages.scene: The king reaches a wide, rushing river. The water roars over rocks. There is no bridge or boat in sight.

pages.caption: The Master-Maid had given him a ball of thread.
pages.scene: The king remembers the ball of thread. He pulls it from his pocket, his hands shaking with desperation.

pages.caption: And he threw it across the river.
pages.scene: The king throws the ball of thread across the river. It arcs through the air, trailing white behind it.

pages.caption: Then he pulled it tight.
pages.scene: The thread catches on the far bank and pulls tight, forming a bridge of white across the rushing water.

pages.caption: And he and the children walked across it as if it were a bridge.
pages.scene: The king steps onto the thread bridge with the children. They walk carefully across the narrow span above the water.

pages.caption: The Master-Maid, who was watching from the castle.
pages.scene: Meanwhile, back at the castle, the Master-Maid watches from a high window. She holds a pair of scissors.

pages.caption: When the giant came to the river, he also threw the ball of thread across.
pages.scene: The giant reaches the riverbank and sees the king crossing. He roars with fury and grabs the thread.

pages.caption: And pulled it tight. But when he set his foot on it.
pages.scene: The giant pulls the thread tight and sets his massive foot upon it. The thread sags under his weight.

pages.caption: The Master-Maid, who was watching from the castle, cut the thread.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid lifts the scissors high. Her face is resolute. The thread stretches across the river below.

pages.caption: And the giant fell into the river.
pages.scene: The thread snaps. The giant plummets into the roaring river below. His arms flail wildly.

pages.caption: And was drowned.
pages.scene: The giant's massive form disappears beneath the churning water. Bubbles rise, then nothing. The river flows on.

pages.caption: Then the king and the children came home.
pages.scene: The king and children stand safely on the far bank. They look back at the river, now empty. The king breathes with relief.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The king walks the road home with the three children holding his hands. The sun sets behind them, painting the sky gold.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The palace comes into view. The king quickens his pace. The children run ahead toward the gate.

pages.caption: And the queen was overjoyed to see them.
pages.scene: The queen stands at the palace door. She sees the children approaching and her hands fly to her face in disbelief.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The queen runs to embrace her children. She holds them tightly, tears streaming down her face. The king watches, smiling.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: The family stands together in the courtyard. The king, queen, and three children are united at last. Light fills the scene.

pages.caption: And the Master-Maid was made queen.
pages.scene: The Master-Maid descends the mountain path, freed from the giant's castle. She walks toward the palace.

pages.caption: None
pages.scene: A grand ceremony in the throne room. The Master-Maid wears a crown and royal robes. The king and queen smile warmly.

pages.caption: And they all lived happily ever after.
pages.scene: The entire court gathers in celebration. Musicians play, banners hang, and the people cheer in the streets below.
